emma: Quick sync — I'm exploring a CP authority slicing model (per-tenant authz gateway) to support sidecarless private endpoints. Wanted to capture tradeoffs before an RFC follow-up.
emma: TL;DR: can we give each tenant a lightweight "authority slice" that holds certs, token introspection cache, and routing policy, but keep the heavy control-plane logic centralized?
jorge: +1 on the idea. Main win is blast-radius isolation and simpler rollback per tenant. But we pay in cert count and extra ephemeral endpoints to route through.
liam: Concern: more slices => more peering/state. If each slice needs connectivity to our central allocator and metrics sink, that's N connections. How do we keep this cheap?
sara: Thoughts: use a single long-lived peering for telemetry/alloc, but short-lived mTLS tunnels for authz checks. So routing plane stays thin.
emma: Exactly — separate concerns: routing + telemetry central, authz slices handle identity and policy. Authz slices should be allowed to be ephemeral and autoscaled.
jorge: Operational example: customer A's slice owns certs for their private endpoints. When a request arrives, edge -> regional relay -> route to central router which uses tenant tag to forward to tenant slice authz (if present) or fallback to shared-legacy-authz.
liam: Fallback is key. We need graceful degredation if tenant slice is down: either central policy or safe-deny. Prefer central permissive for short time windows to avoid an outage.
sara: Agree. Also need a canary strategy for rollout. Maybe: 
```
rollout:
  phase: canary
  fallback: central-authz
  timeout: 250ms
```
if authz slice doesn't respond within timeout, central policy applies.
emma: Perf numbers? If we add one extra network hop for authz, 250–400us for mTLS auth + token check may be OK for most CPU-bound LLM inference calls, but for tail-sensitive low-latency routes we should allow pinning authz to the same host as the relay.
jorge: Another tradeoff: cert lifecycle. Per-tenant certs for endpoint TLS gives strong isolation, but issuing/rotating at scale is heavy. Suggest: short-lived leaf certs minted by a shared CA; authz slice keeps minimal keystore to reissue locally when needed.
liam: That could work. We should design a "mint+cache" flow: central CA mints leaf certs on request, slice caches for TTL, rotates proactively. We must audit issuance frequency to avoid cost/limits.
sara: On routing semantics: we need tokenization of egress IPs when slices live in customer VPCs vs our managed relays. For customer-hosted slices, preserve source IP for audit. For managed slices, we can SNAT but must annotate requests with original source in headers.
emma: Security checklist: KMS integration for slice private keys, HSM optional. Audit logs forwarded to central secure storage. Slice must proof identity to central controlplane via attested mTLS bootstrap.
jorge: Rollback story: if a slice misbehaves we must be able to: 1) disable slice routing 2) switch to central-authz 3) revoke slice certs. All should be a single operator action via console API.
liam: Implementation sketch: add a new resource type in controlplane catalog: authz_slice/{tenant_id}.{region} with fields: endpoint, ca_fingerprint, mode (managed/customer-hosted), failover_policy.
sara: Minimal API example: 
```
POST /v1/slices
body: { tenant: "acme", mode: "managed", policy: { fallback: "central-authz", timeout_ms: 250 } }
```
Response contains ephemeral bootstrap token for the slice to register.
emma: Good. We should also think about metrics QoS: slices should emit aggregated request counters and p95 auth latencies only, avoid shipping raw tokens or identities.
jorge: Operational limits: cap number of active slices per region to control peering and CA pressure. Offer multitenant slices for low-security tenants to reduce N.
liam: Implementation risk: keeping ACLs in sync between central router and slice policy could cause mismatches. Consider a push of policy diffs and a versioned policy id used in routing checks.
sara: Example policy diff flow: central compiles policy v42 for tenant, the router references tenant:42; slice returns a policy-check result including v42 to avoid drift.
emma: One more open item: billing/chargeback for managed slices (extra controlplane CPU, cert ops). Product needs SKU.
jorge: For RFC follow-up: propose prototype with 2 tenants, managed slices in us-west, customer-hosted slice in eu-central to validate peering and source-ip preservation.
liam: I'll spin up a spike repo for slice controller + local test harness this week. @sara can you add the canary+rollback UI hooks to the console spike?
sara: Yup, will add a lightweight toggle and a revoke button.
emma: Thanks all. I'll draft the RFC with architecture diagram and the policy schema. Leaving notes here: diagram should show central router, managed slices, customer slices, fallback path.
infra-bot: deploy-bot noticed: created spike branch "cp-authz-slices" for @liam.
jorge: :thumbsup: good start. We should also measure end-to-end p99 overhead in the spike.
liam: Agreed. I'll post results in this thread when I have numbers.
sern: (typo) -> sorry ignore
emma: tagging this for RFC-queue once the spike has numbers. :thinking:
